summary: Resumed at Phase 19 of plan v5 (plans/06_s5-termination-machinery.md) per handoff 09's continuation order. Landed three more green, sorry-free, CI-clean commits continuing the bespoke Five fuel-induction assembly: (1) modalApplyOneFiveProp_knownWorlds_step + modalApplyOneFive_agree_or_reuse (FiveSimplification.lean) -- the Five analogues of modalApplyOneS5_knownWorlds_step and modalApplyOneS5w_s5SoundSpec, stated directly (no RuleApply/S5SoundSpec abstraction needed since Five has only one shipped rule). (2) modalStepBranchFive_preserves_accReachableInv (FrameSoundness.lean), a direct specialization of the S5 Gen version, plus the missing FiveSimplification.lean import. (3) FiveSoundInv + modalFiveBoxAll_soundIn/modalFiveDiaNegAll_soundIn (FrameSoundness.lean) -- frame-relativized semantic soundness of the two propagation shapes under fiveFC, with the root-triggered arm discharged via hacc + modalFiveBoxAll_root_hasEdge and the non-root arm via accReachableInv_related_five. All three commits are unaffected by the new finding below (propagation-only or purely structural). Continuing to the next item, modalStepBranchFive_preserves_satIn's witness-reuse branch, EXPOSED A NEW, INDEPENDENT SOUNDNESS GAP: modalApplyOneFive's mint arms (T(diamond phi)@w / F(box phi)@w, driven by witnessWorldS5) reuse an existing witness world with NO restriction tying it to the trigger's root/non-root identity or to any recorded edge. The soundness obligation this creates (m.r (f w) (f w') for the new reuse edge) has no accReachableInv_related_five discharge when either endpoint is the root -- exactly the failure mode Route (1) fixed for the PROPAGATION arms, but Route (1) explicitly left the mint arms untouched (reports/07_*: 'Mint-arm fields are untouched'). Diagnosed rigorously with a concrete adversarial two-island RightEuclidean countermodel (mirroring the Fin 3 counterexample's standard of evidence), and confirmed that a naive rule-level guard mirroring Route 1 is NOT a bounded patch: it would let an already-minted (sign,subformula) tag mint a second time whenever a reuse attempt happens to cross the root boundary, breaking the tag-injection termination bound (modalMaxWorld_lt_worldBound_of_S5w, Phase 6/7). Per plan-compliance.md's escalation requirement (a genuine blocker in a .lean file must be raised, not silently patched), Phase 19 is re-marked [BLOCKED] with the full diagnosis recorded in the plan file and a new handoff. No sorry, no vacuous placeholder, no new axiom was introduced at any point.

The S5 deliverable (Phases 0-14) remains complete, green, and committed; per plan R9 it does NOT depend on the Euclidean chain.

blockers.title: mint-arm (witnessWorldS5) reuse soundness gap, independent of the resolved Route-1 propagation gap
blockers.what_failed: modalApplyOneFive's two mint arms (T(diamond phi)@w, F(box phi)@w) call witnessWorldS5 unguarded, reusing any known world (root included) carrying a matching signed formula with no restriction on the trigger/witness's root/non-root identity or on any recorded edge. The soundness proof needs m.r (f trigger) (f witness) for the new reuse edge; accReachableInv_related_five only covers the case where both are non-root.
blockers.evidence: Concrete adversarial two-island RightEuclidean model on Fin 4 (r = {(a,b),(b,b)} union {(c,d),(d,d)}) realizes the failure: each island trivially satisfies RightEuclidean, yet r a d is false, so a model can satisfy diamond phi at f(0)=a via b while independently satisfying phi at an unrelated f(w')=d, with no relatedness between them.
blockers.why_not_a_quick_patch: A rule-level guard mirroring Route 1 (hasEdge check at root, exclude 0 from witness candidacy) would sometimes reject reuse for a (sign,subformula) tag already minted once, forcing a second mint for that same tag from a different trigger -- breaking the tag-injection termination bound the landed Phase 6/7/18 world-bound proof relies on. Fixing this requires re-deriving the termination argument alongside any rule change, not a local patch.
blockers.needed: A dedicated Route-1b research/plan cycle deciding between (a) a rule-level mint-arm guard with the termination bound re-derived from scratch, or (b) a semantic/model-repair argument (Euclidean-closure of m.r plus a new 'closure preserves satisfaction' lemma).
